clue.text: Oldies' get-together that has Bess and ma tangling with a sort of eel

indicators.note: things that are tangling get twisted up together, so the letters of the two names are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a launce is a sand eel

explanation.surface: Two old ladies at a senior citizens' social get into a scuffle over an eel.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSEMBLAUNCE is Spenser's word for an assembly, hence 'Oldies'' meaning it comes from old writers, not from pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblaunce is an archaic word for a gathering, so it is a get-together from the language of old authors.

clue.text: A couple of very small amounts in savings scheme

wordplay.words: A couple of very small amounts
wordplay.note: a sou is an old French coin, used for a tiny amount; a couple of them gives it twice

explanation.surface: Someone puts a couple of pennies at a time into a savings plan.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou-sou is a rotating savings club of Caribbean and West African origin, where members pay in regularly and take turns to draw the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sousou is an informal collective savings arrangement, so it is literally a savings scheme.

clue.text: New among West Africans, it's scanty summer outfit for kids

parts.note: the Susu are a people of Guinea and Sierra Leone

taken as written

explanation.surface: Something new from West Africa turns out to be skimpy summer wear for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunsuit is a brief playsuit that children wear in hot weather, leaving arms and legs bare.

clue.text: Talk in archaic slang? Chap's good in that

parts.note: a chap is a man
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man is good at speaking old thieves' slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To mang is an old cant verb meaning to speak, so it means to talk in a slang now obsolete.

clue.text: Bit of rope in ship's bucket? It'll secure furled sail

indicators.note: the small piece sits in the ship's bucket, enclosed by it

parts.note: a bail is a scoop for throwing water out of a boat

indicators.note: only a bit of the next word is wanted, namely its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of rope

explanation.surface: A length of rope is stowed in the bucket on deck, ready to tie up a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A brail is a small rope on a ship used to truss up a sail against its mast or gaff.

clue.text: Old-fashioned distiller, I'm on northern stream below loch

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is below comes later, so the loch letter goes on top

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for loch
taken as written
a beck is a brook in northern England

explanation.surface: A distiller explains that he works by a northern stream just beneath a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue means placed above, so I'M sits directly over the stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A limbeck is an old form of alembic, a vessel once used for distilling.

clue.text: Dawn not quite rising, university friend appears rarely

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up, so the letters run backwards
not quite all of the word is used: its final letter is dropped

parts.note: sunup is the time of dawn

an ally is a friend
surface padding linking the wordplay to the definition; no letters

explanation.surface: A student's friend, not quite up at dawn, rarely shows his face.
explanation.walkthrough: SUNUP loses its last letter to give SUNU, which is then turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unusually means doing it in a way that seldom happens, so the adverb matches rarely.

clue.text: Merry nest as of old includes rumpy-pumpy

indicators.note: the nest word includes the other inside it, holding it in its middle

parts.note: nid is an old word for a nest, especially a pheasant's
it is slang for sex, as rumpy-pumpy is

explanation.surface: A cheerful love nest of old sees plenty of romping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry' looks like part of the surface description of the nest, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitid means bright and shining, and Chambers also gives it the sense gay or cheerful.

clue.text: Big cat, he-cat that's savaged horse?

indicators.note: something savaged is mauled and torn apart, so these letters are pulled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A big cat, a tom, has mauled a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, which is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Chetah is a variant spelling of cheetah, the spotted hunting animal of the big cat family.

clue.text: Anticoagulant needed in a mucro wound

indicators.note: read as the past of wind, wound means twisted round, so the letters are coiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blood-thinner is called for to treat a wound made by a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: A mucro is a sharp point on a leaf or shell; 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Coumarin and its derivatives such as warfarin are used medically to stop blood from clotting.

clue.text: Architectural decoration

parts.note: read plainly: an ornament on a building
the setter's reading is the same: this is a bare definition with no wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: This is Azed's competition word: it is given only a plain definition, and readers send in their own cryptic clues for it, so there is no wordplay to find.
explanation.definitionFit: A chambranle is an ornamental border framing a door, window or fireplace, a kind of moulding.

clue.text: A free gulp's abused — it's distinctly ominous

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of a free drink is a clear sign of trouble ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Presageful means full of presage or foreboding, so something presageful is plainly a portent of what is coming.

clue.text: Goal for American body-builder?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in US children's games, the home base or goal
second meaning: a big muscular man

explanation.surface: What does an American bodybuilder aim for?
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as one phrase about a gym-goer's ambition, but it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunk is slang for a well-built man, and in American usage it is also the safe home spot in a game of tag.

clue.text: Way, first to last, for one opening another's closet?

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved from the front to the very end

parts.note: a route is a way

explanation.surface: A way for a burglar to open someone else's cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: To out someone is to reveal publicly that they are gay, bringing them out of the closet; 'closet' looks like a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: An outer is a person who publicly exposes someone else's homosexuality, figuratively opening the closet they are in.

clue.text: What goes up at Xmas? Distribution of cards — husband leaves the lot wretchedly for stuffing

indicators.note: the jumbled letters serve as stuffing, packed inside the card word
the husband leaves, so that letter departs from the phrase that follows

parts.note: mise is an old word the setter uses for a laying out of cards
H is the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: wretchedly suggests something in a sorry, disordered state, so the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Christmas scene: cards handed out, and a husband wretchedly leaving all the turkey stuffing to others.
explanation.walkthrough: THE LOT loses its H, and the jumbled remainder goes inside MISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is the sprig hung up indoors at Christmas, so it is something that goes up at Xmas.

clue.text: Constituent of bauxite bits oddly found in scoff

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are found inside the word for scoff

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Odd bits of bauxite turn up in someone's food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' tempts as food, the British slang sense; here it is the verb to jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibbsite is a hydroxide mineral of aluminium and one of the main minerals making up bauxite ore.

clue.text: Ailment in a face that's distinctively pronounced

indicators.note: the illness word sits in the face word, wrapped by it

parts.note: a moue is a pouting face
an ill is an ailment

explanation.surface: A sickness shows in a face that has a very distinctive look.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics mouillé describes a consonant softened or palatalised, such as the Spanish ll, a recognisably distinct pronunciation.

clue.text: Spyhole, one set into masses of coal

explanation.surface: A peephole has been fitted into lumps of coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A judas, or judas hole, is a small peephole in a door through which one can watch unseen, as in a prison cell.

clue.text: Scotsman's box is kept in his outer room

indicators.note: the small word is kept in the room word, stored inside it

parts.note: in a Scottish cottage the but is the outer room and the ben the inner
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot keeps his box in the front room of his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' carries the Scottish sense on to the room: a but and ben is a two-roomed cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Buist is a Scots word for a box or chest, so it is a box in Scottish speech.

clue.text: Vandal maybe, radical holding cheap eatery up

clue.text: Dance, hard for whales to take in, lots abandoned

the whale word takes in the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: cachalots are sperm whales

taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A dance proves hard for whales to master, and many give up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cachalot is another name for the sperm whale; the whales give up their tail, and hard is taken in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Company suite adapted for one into auto-suggestion

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A company's office suite is converted for a hypnotist's use.
explanation.walkthrough: Émile Coué was a French psychologist who promoted self-improvement by auto-suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A Coueist is a follower of Coué's method, someone devoted to curing themselves by auto-suggestion.

clue.text: Percussion instrument rarely used to fluster conductor

parts.note: to favour is to support
E is the abbreviation for English

clue.text: Burning log, good in part as Yuletide warmer

explanation.walkthrough: The yule log is so much the picture that the solver looks for an anagram of log, but the letters lie in sequence across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Glogg is a Scandinavian hot spiced wine drunk at Christmas, a festive drink to warm you up.

clue.text: Sea-goddesses, Greek, doubly aged

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: Greek sea-goddesses who are very old indeed.

explanation.definitionFit: The Graeae were three grey-haired sisters of Greek myth, daughters of sea deities and counted among the goddesses of the sea.

clue.text: Grandpa's pipe (not getting snuff out) alight as of old

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Edge Reds out, allowing crowd in post-apartheid?
